transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (CISO - CrestBank), Ravi Patel (Head of Cloud - CrestBank), Sofia Martinez (Legal), Ethan Zhou (Platform)

Summary:
Quick security and privacy review focused on data handling: prompt/content retention, PII/PHI, confirmation of no training on customer data, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and data residency. Customer requested SOC 2 artifacts and clarifications for pilot and enterprise deployment options (hosted vs private VPC).

Topics:
- Retention and redaction options for prompts and responses
- Statement on model training (no training on customer data) and inference-only usage
- KMS/HSM integration and key lifecycle
- Audit logs, SSO, and RBAC controls
- Data residency and private deployment options (VPC/on-prem)

Action items quick recap at end and next steps recorded.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I think we'll run about 45-60 mins. can do a quick run through security artifacts and then dig into any questions.
[00:12] Laura Kim: Thanks Maya, yeah we have a few targeted questions, mostly around retention and whether data ever leaves our control, also policy on training.
[00:20] Daniel Ortiz: Hi team, I'm Daniel, I'm the solutions engineer. we'll cover kms, audit logs, and some deployment options; i might jump in with architecture diagrams.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Nice to meet you. for context, we're evaluating for a customer support automation pilot. scope includes handling some limited PHI in support transcripts, so PHI and PII handling is critical.
[00:45] Maya Chen: got it. just to set expectations: for the hosted API we have configurable retention windows and an enterprise private option where telemetry and logs can be routed to your VPC or on-prem.
[00:58] Laura Kim: ok and about training - is anything we send used to train your models? we need explicit confirmation.
[01:10] Daniel Ortiz: short answer, no. Redwood policy is inference-only for customer data unless there's an explicit opt-in POC for model improvement which is contractually scoped. we do not train open models on customer prompts.
[01:28] Sofia Martinez: is that in writing somewhere? legal wants a clause for the agreement.
[01:35] Maya Chen: yes, we have a standard clause and we'll include the exact wording in the security pack. i'll add that to the action items.
[01:45] Ethan Zhou: can you clarify what 'no training' means operationally? like do logs ever get pulled into analytics pipelines?
[01:55] Daniel Ortiz: good question. telemetry for platform health is collected, but we segregate and pseudonymize customer content. production data is not used for model training. telemetry references are operational metrics like latency, error rates, counts - not raw prompt text.
[02:15] Ravi Patel: and for compliance we need audit trails showing access to tokens and data. how detailed are the logs?
[02:25] Daniel Ortiz: audit logs include per-request metadata: request id, timestamp, model, route, and token usage. for enterprise customers we can forward logs to your SIEM or to a logging endpoint in your VPC. sensitive payloads can be masked in forwarded logs.
[02:45] Laura Kim: does that include raw prompt/response bodies in the logs?
[02:52] Daniel Ortiz: by default hosted retention may keep prompts for a short debugging window, configurable down to zero retention for enterprise tiers. we can also implement prompt redaction or client-side redaction before sending. we'll include options in the doc we share.
[03:12] Maya Chen: to be explicit: we offer three patterns - 1) default hosted retention (30 days debug window), 2) hosted with no-persistent-content option (prompts not stored), 3) private deployment where customer controls data store and we don't ingest content into Redwood's telemetry.
[03:32] Sofia Martinez: private deployment - do we get full control of keys? we need to ensure keys never leave our KMS.
[03:40] Daniel Ortiz: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS; we support envelope encryption with your KMS/HSM. you bring the keys and we don't have the plaintext. for hosted with customer-managed KMS we use a bring-your-own-key flow and keys stay in your cloud KMS; only wrapped keys are held by our control plane.
[04:05] Ethan Zhou: can you share how key rotation works and whether re-encryption is required?
[04:15] Daniel Ortiz: rotation uses standard practices: new data encrypted with new key, existing ciphertext can be accessed with the old key; re-encryption can be done as part of a migration; we'll provide a tech note.
[04:30] Ravi Patel: latency is a concern, does KMS calls add overhead to inference?
[04:38] Daniel Ortiz: keys are used for storage-level encryption and secrets management, not per-token ops. runtime uses cached keys/kms-wrapped DEKs so impact is minimal.
[04:50] Maya Chen: also notes on SOC2 and ISO: we have a SOC 2 Type II report covering the platform, and in higher tiers we have ISO attestation artifacts - we'll send copies.
[05:05] Laura Kim: great. any SOC scoping around subcontractors or sub-processors? we need a list.
[05:12] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include the sub-processor list in the security pack.
[05:20] Sofia Martinez: on data residency - we have EU customers and some APAC. can you guarantee region residency?
[05:28] Daniel Ortiz: we support region pinning for data, and private deployments can be fully on-prem or in your VPC in the target region. hosted API allows region routing and residency commitments in enterprise contracts.
[05:45] Ravi Patel: about PII/PHI detection - do you provide any built-in redaction or detection tools?
[05:52] Daniel Ortiz: we have an optional pre-processing step that flags likely PII/PHI and can redact client side or server side. for PHI we'd recommend client-side redaction or the private deployment to minimize surface area.
[06:06] Laura Kim: and for HIPAA - do you sign BAAs?
[06:12] Maya Chen: yes, for enterprise customers we can sign BAAs and ensure the private deployment and contractual controls meet HIPAA requirements. we'll include a BAA template in the pack.
[06:25] Ethan Zhou: curious about the claim 'we don't train on customer data' - is that true for both Redwood-verified models and curated open models?
[06:35] Daniel Ortiz: yes, it's a platform policy independent of model catalog. the model artifacts we serve are pre-trained; we don't incorporate customer prompts into model training pipelines. if a customer explicitly engages in a model tuning program, that's a separate, opt-in POC with clear scoping and approvals.
[06:55] Maya Chen: let's talk about retention windows and how we can set them for the pilot. what are you comfortable with?
[07:03] Ravi Patel: for our pilot, we want prompts kept for 7 days for debugging, but responses containing PHI must not be stored at all. is that possible?
[07:12] Daniel Ortiz: yes, that's feasible: mask or drop responses that match PHI patterns, or route them to private storage that you control. we can show sample retention config.
[07:28] Laura Kim: can you also provide an audit trail of who accessed historical logs if we store in your system?
[07:36] Daniel Ortiz: yes, access logs and role-based access are recorded. RBAC integrates with SSO (SAML/SCIM) so you can tie access to identity providers.
[07:50] Sofia Martinez: and do API keys rotate? can we enforce short-lived tokens?
[07:58] Daniel Ortiz: API keys can be rotated; for better security we recommend short-lived credentials using our token service and integrate with your identity provider for sessioned access.
[08:12] Maya Chen: i'll add that we support SCIM for provisioning and SSO via SAML/OIDC.
[08:20] Ethan Zhou: what's the granularity of RBAC? project-level, route-level?
[08:27] Daniel Ortiz: project and route level; you can set role policies for read-only, invoke-only, admin, and custom roles.
[08:38] Ravi Patel: any recommendations for masking PHI at client side?
[08:43] Daniel Ortiz: best practice is to strip structured PHI before sending, replace with tokens, and then rehydrate client-side. if you need to keep raw data for diagnosis, do that in your private store and send samples manually.
[09:00] Laura Kim: ok. about audit and retention - we need to see example logs and a sample retention policy.
[09:08] Maya Chen: we'll attach sample logs and the exact retention config with the security artifacts.
[09:18] Daniel Ortiz: also note that we have an option for end-to-end private deployment (air-gapped) for regulated workloads. in that case Redwood's control plane can be limited or a customer-managed control plane is used.
[09:40] Ravi Patel: that's interesting, might be relevant if we scale beyond pilot.
[09:46] Sofia Martinez: legal will review the BAA and the no-training clause. any standard indemnities?
[09:53] Maya Chen: we have standard liability language; we'll pass the agreement to your team for redlines.
[10:05] Ethan Zhou: technical question - what about KV cache or prompt caching? is any of that persisted?
[10:13] Daniel Ortiz: KV caches are ephemeral on runtime nodes; they are not persisted to object storage. for long-term caching of outputs we use configurable caches, but enterprise private deployments can disable that.
[10:30] Ravi Patel: OK. are there rate limits exposed that might cause logs to be sampled? like for audit completeness?
[10:38] Daniel Ortiz: logs are not sampled for auditing; we can collect all audit events and push them to your SIEM. operational telemetry may be sampled, but audit trails are comprehensive.
[10:52] Laura Kim: what about data deletion requests and e-discovery?
[10:58] Maya Chen: we support deletion at customer request - for hosted customers we can delete any retained artifacts within agreed SLA; for private, you control deletion. we'll include the flow in the doc.
[11:12] Sophia Martinez: can you confirm data used by Redwood's internal monitoring never includes raw prompt text?
[11:19] Daniel Ortiz: monitoring focuses on aggregated metrics; raw prompts are excluded unless we've got a debug toggle which is opt-in and time-limited, and then the customer is notified.
[11:35] Ravi Patel: ok good. any third-party vendors that process data? list please.
[11:41] Maya Chen: yes, that's in the sub-processor list we'll send. common items are cloud infra providers and logging providers.
[11:50] Ethan Zhou: about penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure, do you share reports?
[11:56] Maya Chen: we share summary reports and have a formal vulnerability disclosure program; full pentest reports might be available under NDA - we'll note that.
[12:08] Laura Kim: last question for now - if we start a pilot, what does onboarding look like for security and compliance?
[12:16] Daniel Ortiz: typically 1) sign NDA/BAA, 2) exchange security pack and run quick internal review, 3) set up a private workspace or enterprise project with desired retention settings, 4) optionally set up KMS and VPC peering for private logs.
[12:36] Maya Chen: timeline wise we can have SOC2 and docs to you by Monday (2026-12-20), and schedule the SE deep dive the week after.
[12:50] Ravi Patel: works. any pricing / contract related implications for private deployment?
[12:57] Maya Chen: yes, private and VPC options are typically enterprise-tier and involve a hosting or license fee; we'll include a ballpark in the pricing email.
[13:10] Sofia Martinez: thanks, that's all for questions for now. we'll review docs and come back with redlines.
[13:18] Maya Chen: great. quick recap of next steps and action items:
[13:25] Maya Chen: action item 1 - send SOC2, ISO attestations, sub-processor list, BAA template (Maya) by 2026-12-20.
[13:35] Daniel Ortiz: action item 2 - tech note on KMS/envelope encryption, key rotation, and sample retention configs (Daniel) by 2026-12-22.
[13:45] Ethan Zhou: action item 3 - we'll send our internal compliance checklist and sample dataflow (Ethan) by 2026-12-23.
[13:52] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the pack and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[14:00] Laura Kim: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
